new_statements.rule_in_words: Second-hand areal generalisation only: in the languages of the interior ('center') of south Malakula there is a strong accent on the penultimate syllable and the word-final vowel is heavily reduced. Nasarian is one of Charpentier's interior south-Malakula languages (traditionally spoken inland from Dixon Reef), so the remark plausibly covers it, but neither Charpentier (as quoted) nor Lynch & Crowley say so by name.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Lynch & Crowley add that the phonemic status of the reduced final vowels is unclear.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('next to last syllable'), inferred from Charpentier's wordlist transcription practice (subscript vowels for reduced finals); an areal statement about interior south-Malakula languages, quoted in the Lendamboi section, not in the Nasarian entry. The two modern Nasarian wordlists (ABVD 2015, Vanuatu Voices 2025) are broad IPA with no stress marking.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog nasa1240 = Nasarian (ISO nvh), Charpentier's [nasariana], an interior language of south-west Malakula whose last speakers (5 in 1980; 20 reported 1983 per Wurm) live in the coastal village of Tavendrua = Dixon Reef, alongside Lendamboi/Letemboi speakers. Tryon 1976's 'Dixon Reef II (Ma)' list is Nasarian; 'Dixon Reef I' is Aveteian (dixo1238). Vanuatu Voices 2025 records two doculects, 'Nasarian: Ngava' and 'Nasarian: Wileven'; ABVD's list is 'Nasarian (Wileven tu)'. The only stress remark is an areal one about 'the languages of the center of the island' (interior south Malakula) and is not tied to Nasarian by name.

sources.note: §3.7.25(1) Nasarian, p.84: name [nasariana] from Charpentier 1982a:43; five speakers in 1980 at Tavendrua (Dixon Reef); the only data are Tryon 1976's short 'Dixon Reef II' list (supplied by Charpentier) and Charpentier 1982b's longer vocabulary. No phonology. The sole stress sentence in the book is p.71 fn.6 (Lendamboi section), quoting Charpentier 1982a:63 that in 'the languages of the center of the island, there is a strong tonic accent on the next to last syllable, and the final vowel is so destressed as to become almost unrecognizeable' — areal, Nasarian not named.
